but instead — wait — instead you hand him a ticket, and the ticket *already is a number*. and the number IS the hook. he doesn't search. he just... walks straight to hook 47. every time. doesn't matter if there's four coats or four million coats hanging there, walking to hook 47 takes the same amount of time. that's the whole trick. that's the whole cosmic joke actually — **the address computes itself instead of getting found**.

the "hash function" is the thing that turns your key — a name, a word, whatever — into that number. mash it through some arithmetic, get a number, that number is your hook. so a lookup is just: hash the key (fast, fixed amount of math, doesn't care how big your map is) → jump straight to that slot in the array → done. no walking. no counting. that's why it's O(1) — constant time — the *size of the whole world* doesn't leak into the time it takes to find one coat in it.
